Title: Requirements for Coverage
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
A polysomnogram must be submitted with the initial request for a RAD with those diagnoses that have a polysomnogram requirement in the criteria.
Medicaid shall not accept polysomnograms that are performed by a medical equipment provider . Polysomnograms must be provided according to requirements listed in Clinical Coverage Policy 1A-20, Sleep Studies and Polysomnography Services , on Medicaid's website: https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/.
The polysomnogram must be based on a minimum of two (2) hours of recorded sleep time without the use of a CPAP or RAD device, reported by the polysomnogram. The polysomnogram must include sleep staging and other sleep parameters such as airflow, respiratory effort, and oxygen saturation by oximetry.
If the polysomnogram criteria listed above are not met, claims submitted for reimbursement of a RAD and related accessories are denied as not medically necessary.
For an item to be covered by Medicaid a written signed and dated order from the 'treating physician' must be received by the supplier before the CMN/PA form is submitted for prior approval. The treating physician is one who is qualified by virtue of experience and training in non-invasive respiratory assistance, to order and monitor the use of the respiratory assist devices.
If there is a discontinuation of the RAD at any time, the provider is expected to determine that the RAD has been discontinued and stop billing for the equipment and related accessories.
A RAD with a back-up rate is not medically necessary if the primary diagnosis is OSA.
Initial Prior Approval: For a RAD to be covered, the treating physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner, shall fully document in the beneficiary's clinical health record those symptoms characteristic of sleepassociated hypoventilation, such as daytime hypersomnolence, excessive fatigue, morning headache, cognitive dysfunction, or dyspnea, etc.
Initial prior approval for a RAD is given for a period of six (6) months .
Note: A RAD without a back-up rate is reimbursed as a rental only and not to exceed a total of monthly rental payments equal to the purchase price. A RAD with a back-up rate is reimbursed as a continuous rental item.
Renewal Prior Approval: For renewal prior approval and continued coverage of the RAD beyond the first six (6) months of therapy, no sooner than the fifth (5 th ) month after initiating therapy:
The provider shall obtain a statement of compliance from the treating physician declaring that the beneficiary is using the device an average of four (4) hours per 24-hour period this must be submitted along with the CMN/PA form request for renewal. Failure of the beneficiary to be consistently using the RAD for an average of four (4) hours per the 24-hour period by the time of the reevaluation would represent non-compliant use and constitute reason for Medicaid to deny continued coverage as not medically necessary; and
A statement must be submitted by the physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner indicating the progress of relevant symptoms and that the RAD is still medically necessary.
Note: A non-heated or heated humidifier is covered by Medicaid with the use of a RAD. The treating physician shall specify which type of humidifier the beneficiary is to use.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:Attachment D
Title: Attachment D: Requesting Unlisted DME and Supplies for Adults
Section: Attachment D
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
In compliance with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Home Health Final Rule, 42 CFR Part 440.70, please follow these guidelines when requesting medical necessity reviews for DME and supplies for adults not listed in Attachment A, Section C or the DME fee schedule.
a . The general requirements and criteria set forth in clinical coverage policy 5A-2 must be met.
This includes, but is not limited to:
The item being requested must fit the definition of durable medical equipment or supplies;
The beneficiary must be enrolled in the Medicaid program and be eligible for the item;
The provider must be enrolled in the Medicaid program with an appropriate taxonomy;
The requested item must be safe, effective, economical and not intended for the convenience of the beneficiary, the beneficiary's caregiver, or the provider;
The item must be medical in nature, generally recognized as an accepted method of treatment, and must not be experimental or investigational;
The item must be ordered by a physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner; and
The item must be medically necessary to maintain or improve a beneficiary's medical, physical or functional level, and appropriate for use in any non-institutional setting in which normal life activities take place;
A documented face-to-face encounter with the beneficiary and the ordering physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner related to the primary reason the beneficiary requires the item must have occurred no more than six months prior to the initiation of durable medical equipment or supplies; and
The beneficiary's need for the item must be reviewed by the ordering physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner at least annually.
If the provider determines that the applicable requirements and criteria set forth in clinical coverage policy 5A-2 have been met, then the provider may submit a completed Certificate of Medical Necessity/Prior Approval (CMN/PA form) and the usual supportive prior approval documentation, through NCTracks for a medical necessity review.
Providers may request non-covered, unlisted, or restricted items using their identifiable HCPCS code (such as E1012). If no HCPCS code exists, providers may use the miscellaneous combination K0108/W4005 for wheelchair accessories only, and for non-wheelchair items, the miscellaneous combination E1399/W4047.
Items approved by this procedure may be manually priced. Please include the appropriate manual pricing documentation with the prior approval request (see May 2017 Medicaid Bulletin for details).
Providers should expect medical necessity reviews using this procedure to take longer than usual.
Claims for items approved using this procedure should also be submitted through NCTracks.
If denied, the provider and beneficiary will be notified, and normal beneficiary appeal rights will apply.
Providers will be notified if the device requested is covered by a different Medicaid policy area or waiver program.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:5.5
Title: 5.5 Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies Limitations
Section: 5.5
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched limitation.
Content:
Medicaid may place appropriate limits, based on medical necessity criteria, on Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies. When the prescribing physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner, orders equipment or supplies beyond these limits, the DME provider shall seek prior approval for these items through NCTracks.
A PA request for an override of a quantity limit, or lifetime expectancy must include the usual PA documentation ( Subsections 5.2 and 5.3 ) along with the following additional information:
The item being requested for an override clearly marked on the CMN/PA form.
The type of override (quantity limit, or lifetime expectancy) clearly stated.
An explanation of the medical necessity for the override from the physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner, or therapist.
Override PA requests are reviewed for medical necessity as per usual PA review timelines. Override PA review outcomes are communicated to providers and beneficiaries in the same way as a typical PA request.
Refer to Attachment A, Section C: Procedure Code(s) for a listing of the established lifetime expectancies and quantity limitations for Durable Medical Equipment and Supplies. To request a medical necessity review for an item not listed, refer to sections 1.2 , 2.2 and Attachment D for instructions.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:5.8
Title: 5.8 Servicing and Repairing Medical Equipment
Section: 5.8
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched not covered.
Content:
Service and repair of medical equipment is handled in one of three ways:
Rental Equipment: Service and repairs are provided as part of the rental arrangement with no additional charge to Medicaid.
Purchased Equipment Warranty: Service and repairs are handled under any warranty coverage an item may have. If there is no warranty, providers may request prior approval to perform the needed service and repairs by submitting a completed CMN/PA form with a repair estimate to NCTracks. The estimate must show a breakdown of charges for parts and the number of hours of labor. No charge is allowed for pick-up or delivery of the item or for the assembly of Medicaid reimbursed parts.
Purchased Equipment Non-Warranty: Service or repair is covered if the equipment is owned by the beneficiary and if the repair is not covered under the warranty. A repair estimate must be provided. The estimate must show a breakdown of charges for parts and the number of hours of labor. No charge is allowed for pick-up or delivery, for the assembly of Medicaid reimbursed parts or for freight or the provider's travel time or expenses. All the following information must be documented in block 30 of the CMN/PA form:
The description and HCPCS code of the item being serviced or repaired.
The age of the item.
The number of times the item has been previously repaired.
The current replacement cost.
Note: Providers shall have emergency repair service available 24-hours a day, seven days a week for any life-sustaining equipment they provide.
Note: Medicaid shall not cover maintenance or service contracts.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:_s48
Title: Requirements for Coverage:
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched not covered.
Content:
A polysomnogram must be submitted with the initial request for prior approval of a CPAP or BiLevel device.
Note: Medicaid shall not accept polysomnograms that are performed by a medical equipment provider .
Polysomnograms must be provided according to requirements listed in Medicaid's Clinical Coverage Policy 1A-20, Sleep Studies and Polysomnography Services , on Medicaid's website: https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/.
The polysomnogram must be based on a minimum of two (2) hours of recorded sleep time without the use of the CPAP or BiLevel device, reported by the polysomnogram. The polysomnogram must include sleep staging and other sleep parameters such as airflow, respiratory effort, and oxygen saturation by oximetry.
If the polysomnogram criteria listed above are not met, claims submitted for reimbursement of the CPAP or BiLevel device and related accessories are not medically necessary, and therefore not covered.
For an item to be covered by Medicaid, a written signed and dated order from the treating physician must be received by the supplier before the CMN/PA form is submitted for prior approval. If the supplier submits a CMN/PA form without first receiving the completed order, the prior approval request is denied as not medically necessary.
If there is discontinuation of the CPAP or BiLevel device at any time, the provider is expected to determine this, and stop billing for the equipment and related accessories.
Auto-titrating CPAP devices are billed the same as a CPAP device.
A non-heated or heated humidifier is covered by Medicaid with the use of a CPAP or BiLevel. The treating physician shall specify which type of humidifier the beneficiary is to use.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:5.8
Title: 5.8 Servicing and Repairing Medical Equipment
Section: 5.8
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-01
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)

Content:
Service and repair of medical equipment is handled in one of three ways:
Rental Equipment: Service and repairs are provided as part of the rental arrangement with no additional charge to Medicaid.
Purchased Equipment Warranty: Service and repairs are handled under any warranty coverage an item may have. If there is no warranty, providers may request prior approval to perform the needed service and repairs by submitting a completed CMN/PA form with a repair estimate to NCTracks. The estimate must show a breakdown of charges for parts and the number of hours of labor. No charge is allowed for pick-up or delivery of the item or for the assembly of Medicaid reimbursed parts.
Purchased Equipment Non-Warranty: Service or repair is covered if the equipment is owned by the beneficiary and if the repair is not covered under the warranty. A repair estimate must be provided. The estimate must show a breakdown of charges for parts and the number of hours of labor. No charge is allowed for pick-up or delivery, for the assembly of Medicaid reimbursed parts or for freight or the provider's travel time or expenses. All the following information must be documented in block 30 of the CMN/PA form:
The description and HCPCS code of the item being serviced or repaired.
The age of the item.
The number of times the item has been previously repaired.
The current replacement cost.
Note: Providers shall have emergency repair service available 24-hours a day, seven days a week for any life-sustaining equipment they provide.
Note: Medicaid shall not cover maintenance or service contracts.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5A-2:5.9
Title: 5.9 Replacing Medical Equipment
Section: 5.9
Policy: 5A-2
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-01
Citation link: [Respiratory Equipment and Supplies](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5a-2-respiratory-equipment-and-supplies/download?attachment)

Content:
Medicaid may consider replacing the item, when repairing is no longer cost-effective and the item is out of warranty, Refer to Attachment A, Section C: Procedure Codes(s). To request a medical necessity review for an item not listed, see sections 1.2 , 2.2 and Attachment D for instructions.
Note: When requesting prior approval for the replacement of an item before its usual life expectancy has ended, explain on the CMN/PA form why the replacement is needed.
Specific documentation, in addition to the prescription and CMN/PA form, is required in the following situations:
In cases of equipment loss or damage beyond repair, a letter from the social worker, case manager or child service coordinator explaining the circumstances.
In cases of theft, a copy of the police report or a letter from the appropriate person with knowledge of the occurrence, such as the school principal, social worker, etc.
In cases of equipment destruction by fire, a copy of the fire report.
In cases of wide-spread natural disasters, documentation is accepted from any of the entities listed above or from the NC Division of Emergency Management, Federal Emergency Management Agency, American Red Cross, the National Guard or other appropriate state or local authorities and agencies on the ground in the affected areas.

per_question.question: Does Policy 1-H authorize routine general-wellness telehealth visits without a specific clinical indication?
per_question.agent_answer:
**No.** Policy 1-H does not authorize telehealth simply for routine, general wellness without a clinical basis. It permits eligible services to be delivered remotely, but requires telehealth care to meet the same quality standard as in-person care and directs readers to the eligible-service and provider rules. [Policy 1-H § Telehealth, Virtual Communications, and Remote Patient Monitoring Services Covered in Clinical Coverage Policy 1-H](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment)

Coverage under Policy 1-H requires medical necessity and a service that is individualized, specific, and consistent with symptoms or a confirmed diagnosis of the illness or injury being treated; it also cannot be primarily for convenience. [Policy 1-H § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) Medicaid does not cover a service when the beneficiary does not meet the policy’s Section 3 criteria. [Policy 1-H § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment)

For a beneficiary under 21, EPSDT can override some policy limitations only where the provider documents that the service is medically necessary to correct or ameliorate an identified defect, illness, or health condition; that still does not support a visit with no clinical indication. [Policy 1-H § 2.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment)

It accurately explains that telehealth is a modality for delivering specific covered clinical services, requires medical necessity, and must meet Section 3.1 criteria (individualized, specific, consistent with symptoms or confirmed diagnosis, not primarily for convenience). The agent cites specific sections (3.1, 4.1, 2.2.1) with direct links, all of which are supported by the Evidence block. The EPSDT discussion is accurate and supported by the evidence. No hallucinated claims are present - all cited sections and their content match the Evidence block. The answer is thorough, well-cited, and would be accepted by a Medicaid policy expert.

Section: 2.2.1

Reason: EPSDT special-provision section that may modify policy limitations for beneficiaries under 21.
Content:
42 U.S.C. § 1396d(r) [1905(r) of the Social Security Act]
Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) is a federal Medicaid requirement that requires the state Medicaid agency to cover services, products, or procedures for Medicaid beneficiary under 21 years of age if the service is medically necessary health care to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition [health problem] identified through a screening examination (includes any evaluation by a physician or other licensed practitioner).
This means EPSDT covers most of the medical or remedial care a child needs to improve or maintain his or her health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.
Amended Date: February 15, 2025
Amended Date: February 15, 2025
Medically necessary services will be provided in the most economic mode, as long as the treatment made available is similarly efficacious to the service requested by the beneficiary's physician, therapist, or other licensed practitioner; the determination process does not delay the delivery of the needed service; and the determination does not limit the beneficiary's right to a free choice of providers.
EPSDT does not require the state Medicaid agency to provide any service, product or procedure:
that is unsafe, ineffective, or experimental or investigational.
that is not medical in nature or not generally recognized as an accepted method of medical practice or treatment.
Service limitations on scope, amount, duration, frequency, location of service, and other specific criteria described in clinical coverage policies may be exceeded or may not apply as long as the provider's documentation shows that the requested service is medically necessary 'to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition' [health problem]; that is, provider documentation shows how the service, product, or procedure meets all EPSDT criteria, including to correct or improve or maintain the beneficiary's health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.

per_question.question: Does NEMT (Non-Emergency Medical Transportation) cover transportation to non-medical errands such as grocery shopping?
per_question.agent_answer:
**No.** NC Medicaid NEMT does not cover transportation for non-medical errands such as grocery shopping. NEMT is limited to trips to the nearest appropriate medical provider for a Medicaid-covered service, and the trip’s **primary reason must be medical care**. [Policy MA-2910 § IV.A, Medicaid Covered Services](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2910-.pdf) [Policy MA-2910 § II.A, Medicaid only pays for transportation](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2910-.pdf)

This rule applies under both the Aged, Blind, and Disabled and Family and Children NEMT manuals. [Policy MA-3550 § IV.A, Medicaid Covered Services](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-3550-.pdf) [Policy MA-3550 § II.A, Medicaid only pays for transportation](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-3550-.pdf)

The current manuals were revised in March 2026; the latest 2026 change notices updated reimbursement-rate charts rather than this medical-purpose limitation. [Policy MA-2910 Change Notice 04-26](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/CN-04-26-ABD.docx.pdf) Policy MA-3550 Change Notice 04-26

scores.explanation: The agent's answer is factually correct and complete - NEMT does not cover grocery shopping or non-medical errands, and the primary reason for the trip must be medical care. The answer correctly cites both MA-2910 and MA-3550, and accurately notes that 2026 amendments updated rate charts rather than the medical-purpose limitation. The citation quality is good but not precise at the section level (e.g., 'MA-2910 § IV.A' rather than the exact section IDs). Minor hallucination concern: the agent references 'March 2026' revision date which is supported by evidence ('REVISED 03/16/2026'), and the amendment content about rate charts is supported by the getAmendments evidence. The section citations like '§ IV.A' and '§ II.A' are somewhat imprecise but directionally correct based on the evidence (Section IV.A is 'Medicaid Covered Services' and Section II.A is 'Medicaid only pays for transportation'). Overall this is a solid, accurate answer that a Medicaid policy expert would accept.

uncited_claims: NEMT is limited to trips to the nearest appropriate medical provider for a Medicaid-covered service, and the trip’s **primary reason must be medical care**.

Content:
Ambulance transportation that is not medically necessary is arranged by the local agency.
On very rare occasions, an ambulance is the only means of transport for a beneficiary who does not meet the criteria for medically necessary ambulance transportation.
To accommodate such beneficiaries, the local agency must contract with an ambulance company or negotiate a trip cost with the ambulance company on an as needed basis.
The local agency must negotiate a rate for ambulance transport that does not include basic life support or advanced life support services.
Example : Individual is morbidly obese to the point of not being able to walk or climb stairs. The ambulance company is not providing a 'medical service' in this instance; therefore, they will submit a claim as a NEMT ambulance transportation, not medically necessary.

ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-2910:url-38e3dfdc4566:_s5
Title: A. Medicaid only pays for transportation:
Policy: MA-2910
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-2910 – NON-EMERGENCY MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION (NEMT)](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2910-.pdf)

Content:
By the least expensive mode available and appropriate for the beneficiary,
To the nearest appropriate medical provider,
To a Medicaid-covered service provided by a NC enrolled Medicaid provider (with exceptions outlined in this policy). A Medicaid covered service is a service that is covered under the NC Medicaid program. Refer to Division of Health Benefits (DHB) clinical coverage policy.
The following individuals/services are not Eligible for NEMT:
MQB-Q, B, or E only beneficiaries
Beneficiaries in deductible status -An applicant/ beneficiary is not eligible for Medicaid transportation assistance until their deductible is met.
North Carolina Health Choice (NCHC) beneficiaries
Nursing home beneficiaries -The facility is responsible for providing transportation to their patients.
Individuals receiving certain mental health services: Transportation costs are included in
MA-2910
the Medicaid provider's fee; therefore, beneficiaries are not eligible for NEMT to these services. See below.
Innovations Waiver covered services that have transportation included in the Medicaid provider's fee:

| Innovation Services               | CODE    |
|:----------------------------------|:--------|
| Day Supports - Individual         | T2021   |
| DaySupports - Group               | T2021HQ |
| Supported Employment - Individual | H2025   |
| Supported Employment - Group      | H2025HQ |

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-2910:url-38e3dfdc4566:_s10
Title: A. Medicaid Covered Services
Policy: MA-2910
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-2910 – NON-EMERGENCY MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION (NEMT)](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2910-.pdf)

Content:
Non-Emergency Medical transportation is only provided for Medicaid covered services and when the primary reason for the trip is medical care. Consult the
Medicaid Clinical Coverage Manual for information on the service in question (DHB Clinical Coverage Policy).
Example 1: Beneficiary participates in a sheltered workshop program at a facility that provides medical services. Because the primary reason for the trip is to participate in the sheltered workshop program, transportation would not be covered even though a medical service is received during the course of the day.
Example 2: Beneficiary is a child who receives medical services while at school. Transportation would not be provided to the school because a medical service is not the primary reason for the trip.

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-2910:url-38e3dfdc4566:_s45
Title: A. Transportation Requests
Policy: MA-2910
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-2910 – NON-EMERGENCY MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION (NEMT)](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-2910-.pdf)

Content:
The beneficiary must contact the transportation coordinator to request assistance for all medical service trips during the certification period. The request may include multiple trips.
All requests for medical transportation by Medicaid beneficiaries, regardless of program, must be documented and treated as trip requests, even if it appears obvious that the individual will not be entitled to NEMT for the trip requested.
Example 1: Individual calls and requests transportation to their doctor for a March 9 th  appointment. IMC verifies eligibility and determines that the individual receives MQB-B only. The trip request must be logged.
Example 2: Individual calls and requests to be transported to the pharmacy on April 16. IMC determines that this individual is not currently eligible in any Medicaid program. There is no need to log this trip request.

per_question.question: Does the CAP/DA waiver cover a beneficiary's room and board in their own home?
per_question.agent_answer:
**No.** CAP/DA is designed to provide specified home- and community-based waiver services that help eligible adults remain in or return to a community setting; it does **not** list a beneficiary’s ordinary room and board in their own home as a CAP/DA-covered service. The waiver’s current service list includes such items as in-home aide services, meal preparation and delivery, equipment/modifications, respite, personal assistance, and case management—not rent, mortgage, utilities, or other room-and-board costs. [Policy 3K-2 § CAP/DA Waiver Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) CAP/DA also does not cover a service when the beneficiary does not meet the applicable eligibility or coverage criteria, among other general exclusions. [Policy 3K-2 § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

This is based on the current Policy 3K-2, effective September 1, 2025, as revised under the September 1, 2025 all-sections-and-attachments change notice. [Policy 3K-2 Change Notice](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

The answer cites Policy 3K-2 sections 1.0 and 4.1, which are supported by the evidence. However, the claim that 'rent, mortgage, utilities, or other room-and-board costs' are explicitly excluded is a slight embellishment — the evidence shows the service list doesn't include these items, but the policy doesn't explicitly name them as excluded in the sections provided. Reason: Scope or description section for the yes/no coverage question.
Content:
The Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA) is a Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waiver authorized under section1915(c) of the Social Security Act and complies with 42 CFR § 440.180, Home and community-based waiver services. This waiver program provides a cost-effective alternative to institutionalization for a beneficiary, in a specified target population, who is at risk for institutionalization if specialized waiver services were not available. These services allow this targeted individual to remain in or return to a home and community-based setting.
HCBS waivers are approved by Centers of Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) for a specified time. The waiver establishes the requirements for program administration and funding. Federal regulations for HCBS waivers are found in 42 CFR Part 441 Subpart G, Home and Community-Based Services: Waiver Requirements. NC Medicaid can renew or amend the waiver with the approval of CMS. CMS may exercise its authority to terminate the waiver when it believes the waiver is not operated properly. The CAP/DA HCBS (referred to as CAP/DA for the purpose of this policy) is a waiver that serves an adult with disabilities 18 years of age and older who is at risk of institutionalization. To receive services from this waiver program as listed on the service plan, the individual shall meet the Medicaid eligibility requirements for long-term care.
Pursuant to 42 CFR§ 431.10, NC Medicaid is the administrative authority of the waiver and outlines the policies and procedures governing the waiver. NC Medicaid appoints local entities to provide the day-to-day operation of the waiver to ensure the primary six waiver assurances are met.

### 4.2.2 Specific Criteria Not Covered by Medicaid
None Apply.

### Subsection 5.4.2;
The case management entity (CME) has been unable to establish contact with the beneficiary or their responsible party to monitor the provision of care to ensure the health and well-being for more than 90 calendar days, despite more than two (2) verbal and (2) written attempts;
The beneficiary's Medicaid eligibility is terminated and cannot be reactivated;
The beneficiary's Medicaid is not active; in one of the non-approved Medicaid categories; or is in a Medicaid sanction period;
The beneficiary or responsible party demonstrates, as evidence through written correspondence, a continued inability or unwillingness to adhere to the rights and responsibilities as outlined in the 'Beneficiary Rights and Responsibilities' form signed by the beneficiary during the admission and readmission process in Appendix E ;
The beneficiary enters a non-eligible residential placement, nursing facility for a short-term rehabilitation stay or long-term nursing facility stay. When a beneficiary enters a skilled nursing facility or rehabilitation center for a short-term rehabilitative stay, CAP/DA services are suspended until discharged from the facility. The beneficiary is eligible to be reinstated into the program upon discharge. A beneficiary is eligible to be reinstated upon discharge if the short-term rehabilitation does not exceed 90 calendar days of placement;
The annual paid expenditure exceeds the average per capita cost of expenditure for an individual receiving institutional services and the ongoing average cost of care cannot be provided at a cost less than the average cost of institutional services;
The applicant or active beneficiary's currently approved services (Medicaid and non-Medicaid) are meeting assessed care needs, and the applicant or beneficiary is determined to not have a reasonable need for one waiver service if the home and community-based services were terminated (refer to Appendix F );
When the only assessed need is a home or vehicle modification or assistive technology, and evidence is provided of the installation and a claim has been adjudicated by NCTracks, and no other waiver service was assessed to be needed at the next scheduled quarterly monitoring visit;
The applicant or active beneficiary does not exercise their agreement through freedom of choice to participate in the CAP/DA waiver;
The beneficiary has not completed an emergency or disaster plan within 30 calendar days of the approved service plan;
The beneficiary or responsible party cannot demonstrate willingness or intellectual capability to assume the responsibilities of consumer-directed care as evidenced by re-completion of self-assessment questionnaires, training and orientation and coaching and guidance;
The beneficiary does not sign the person-centered service plan to agree to the service interventions to maintain community placement to avoid an institutional placement; or
the beneficiary does not reside in an approved primary private residence or other designated location.
Note: The beneficiary shall be eligible to participate in the CAP/DA waiver when in deductible status; however, CAP/DA services are not reimbursed by Medicaid until Medicaid services are incurred and documented through receipts or invoices.

### 4.2.1 Specific Criteria Not Covered by Medicaid
Medicaid shall not cover CAP / DA participation and services for any one of the following:
The Community Alternatives Program (CAP) special indicator code has not been entered or has been removed from the eligibility information system (NC FAST) and cannot be reentered;
The HCBS Service Request Form is incomplete or has been denied; or a request for additional information was not received within the specified timeframe;
The required annual assessment recertification was not approved or completed within 12 months of the annual assessment at no fault of the beneficiary or applicant;
If an assessment of medical and functional needs has not been completed by a nurse or social worker to determine reasonable indication of need of CAP/DA services at no fault of the beneficiary or applicant, defined in Appendix F ;

Title: 2.2.1 EPSDT Special Provision: Exception to Policy Limitations for a Medicaid Beneficiary under 21 Years of Age
Section: 2.2.1
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: EPSDT special-provision section that may modify policy limitations for beneficiaries under 21.
Content:
42 U.S.C. § 1396d(r) [1905(r) of the Social Security Act]
Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) is a federal Medicaid requirement that requires the state Medicaid agency to cover services, products, or procedures for Medicaid beneficiary under 21 years of age if the service is medically necessary health care to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition [health problem] identified through a screening examination ** (includes any evaluation by a physician or other licensed clinician).This means EPSDT covers most of the medical or remedial care a child needs to improve or maintain their health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.
Medically necessary services shall be provided in the most economic mode, as long as the treatment made available is similarly efficacious to the service requested by the beneficiary's physician, therapist, or other licensed practitioner; the determination process does not delay the delivery of the needed service; and the determination does not limit the beneficiary's right to a free choice of providers.
EPSDT does not require the state Medicaid agency to provide any service, product or procedure:
that is unsafe, ineffective, or experimental or investigational.
that is not medical in nature or not generally recognized as an accepted method of medical practice or treatment.
Service limitations on scope, amount, duration, frequency, location of service, and other specific criteria described in clinical coverage policies may be exceeded or may not apply as long as the provider's documentation shows that the requested service is medically necessary 'to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition' [health problem]; that is, provider documentation shows how the service, product, or procedure meets all EPSDT criteria, including to correct or improve or maintain the beneficiary's health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:1.0
Title: 1.0 Description of the Procedure, Product, or Service
Section: 1.0
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-09-01
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

Content:
The Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA) is a Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waiver authorized under section1915(c) of the Social Security Act and complies with 42 CFR § 440.180, Home and community-based waiver services. This waiver program provides a cost-effective alternative to institutionalization for a beneficiary, in a specified target population, who is at risk for institutionalization if specialized waiver services were not available. These services allow this targeted individual to remain in or return to a home and community-based setting.
HCBS waivers are approved by Centers of Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) for a specified time. The waiver establishes the requirements for program administration and funding. Federal regulations for HCBS waivers are found in 42 CFR Part 441 Subpart G, Home and Community-Based Services: Waiver Requirements. NC Medicaid can renew or amend the waiver with the approval of CMS. CMS may exercise its authority to terminate the waiver when it believes the waiver is not operated properly. The CAP/DA HCBS (referred to as CAP/DA for the purpose of this policy) is a waiver that serves an adult with disabilities 18 years of age and older who is at risk of institutionalization. To receive services from this waiver program as listed on the service plan, the individual shall meet the Medicaid eligibility requirements for long-term care.
Pursuant to 42 CFR§ 431.10, NC Medicaid is the administrative authority of the waiver and outlines the policies and procedures governing the waiver. NC Medicaid appoints local entities to provide the day-to-day operation of the waiver to ensure the primary six waiver assurances are met.

Content:
Medicaid shall not cover the procedure, product, or service related to this policy when:
the beneficiary does not meet the eligibility requirements listed in Section 2.0;
the beneficiary does not meet the criteria listed in Section 3.0;
the procedure, product, or service duplicates another provider's procedure, product, or service; or
the procedure, product, or service is experimental, investigational, or part of a clinical trial.

per_question.question: Is private-duty nursing covered under NC Medicaid Policy 3G-1 for adult beneficiaries who do not meet medical-complexity criteria?
per_question.agent_answer:
**No.** For beneficiaries age 21 or older, Policy 3G-1 covers private-duty nursing (PDN) only when it is medically appropriate and medically necessary **and** the beneficiary meets the policy’s coverage criteria. [Policy 3G-1 § 1.0](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3g-1-private-duty-nursing-beneficiaries-age-21-and-older/download?attachment) Medicaid does not cover PDN when the beneficiary fails to meet the Section 3.0 criteria. [Policy 3G-1 § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3g-1-private-duty-nursing-beneficiaries-age-21-and-older/download?attachment)

For adults, those criteria expressly include meeting the health criteria in § 3.3, along with eligibility requirements, physician order, prior approval, a qualifying home-based purpose, and an available trained informal caregiver. [Policy 3G-1 § 3.2.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3g-1-private-duty-nursing-beneficiaries-age-21-and-older/download?attachment) Section 3.3 requires the beneficiary to meet the Level 1 medical criteria—such as specified ventilator, respiratory, skilled-nursing-intervention, and organ-system-deficiency requirements—before PDN can be authorized; Level 2 requires all Level 1 criteria plus an additional listed condition. [Policy 3G-1 § 3.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3g-1-private-duty-nursing-beneficiaries-age-21-and-older/download?attachment)

The policy’s EPSDT exception applies to beneficiaries **under 21**, not adults. [Policy 3G-1 § 2.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3g-1-private-duty-nursing-beneficiaries-age-21-and-older/download?attachment)

scores.explanation: The agent's answer correctly states that PDN is not covered for adult beneficiaries who do not meet the medical-complexity criteria. It accurately identifies the relevant sections: §1.0 (description), §4.1 (general criteria not covered), §3.2.2 (Medicaid additional criteria covered, including health criteria in §3.3), §3.3.1 (Level 1 criteria including ventilator dependency, respiratory requirements, skilled nursing interventions, organ system deficiencies), §3.3.2 (Level 2 criteria), and §2.2.1 (EPSDT applies only to under-21 beneficiaries). All cited sections and their content are supported by the Evidence block. The answer is precise, well-structured, and cites specific policy sections with links. The only minor difference from the reference answer is that the agent does not mention that care needs are addressed through lower-intensity benefits like personal care services, but this omission does not constitute an error. No hallucinations are present.

Reason: Scope or description section for the yes/no coverage question.
Content:
Private Duty Nursing (PDN) is a substantial, complex, and continuous skilled nursing care that is considered supplemental to the care provided to a beneficiary by the beneficiary's family, foster parents, and delegated caregivers, as applicable Private Duty Nursing services is defined by 42CFR 440.80. Private Duty Nursing services are for a beneficiary who may require more individual and continuous care than is available from a visiting nurse or routinely provided by the nursing staff of the hospital or skilled nursing facility.
PDN care must be medically appropriate and medically necessary for the beneficiary to be covered by NC Medicaid. PDN services are provided:
Only in the beneficiary's private primary residence;
Under the direction of a written individualized plan of care;
Authorized by the beneficiary's primary physician; and
PDN services must be rendered by a registered nurse (RN) or licensed practical nurse (LPN) who is licensed by the North Carolina Board of Nursing (NCBON) and employed by a state licensed and accredited home care agency.

Content:

### 4.2.1 Specific Criteria Not Covered by Medicaid
None Apply.

### 4.2.2 Medicaid Additional Criteria Not Covered
Medicaid shall not cover PDN if any of the following are true:
the beneficiary is receiving medical care in a hospital, nursing facility, outpatient facility, or residential-type medical setting where licensed personnel are employed;
the beneficiary is a resident of an adult care home, group home, family care home, or nursing facility;
the service is for custodial, companion, respite services (short-term relief for the caregiver) or medical or community transportation services;
the nursing care activities rendered can be delegated to unlicensed personnel (Nurse Aide I or Nurse Aide II), according to 21 NCAC 36.0401 and 21 NCAC 36.0221(b);
the purpose of having a licensed nurse with the beneficiary is for observation or monitoring in case an intervention is required;
the service is for the beneficiary or caregiver to go on overnight trips away from the beneficiary's private primary residence. Note: Short-term absences from the primary private residence that allow the beneficiary to receive medical care in an alternate setting for a short period of time, and therapeutic leave requests may be allowed if the following are true: PDN is not provided for respite, PDN is not provided in an institutional setting, and when PDN is provided according to nurse and home care licensure regulations;
services are provided exclusively in the school
the beneficiary does not have informal caregiver support available as per Subsection 3.2.2.f;
the beneficiary is receiving home health nursing services or respiratory therapy treatment (except as allowed under clinical coverage policy 10D, Independent Practitioners Respiratory Therapy Services ) during the same hours of the day as PDN;
the beneficiary is receiving infusion therapy services as found under the clinical coverage policy 3H-, Home Infusion Therapy (HIT) program; or
Amended Date: : May 15, 2024
the beneficiary is receiving hospice services as found under clinical coverage policy 3D, Hospice Services , except as those services may apply to children under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act. H.R.3590
the beneficiary is receiving services from other formal support programs (such as NC Innovations) during the same hours of the day as PDN.

Content:
[Container heading with 4 child sections:]

### 5.3.3 Medical Settings
PDN is not covered for a beneficiary in a hospital, nursing facility, outpatient facility, or residential-type medical setting where licensed personnel are employed and have prescribed responsibility for providing care for the designated beneficiary.

### 5.3.4 Weaning of a Medical Device
NC Medicaid or its designee may authorize PDN services for a brief period after the beneficiary no longer requires the medical device to compensate for loss of a vital body function. Within 10 business days, the PDN service provider shall notify NC Medicaid and submit the DMA -3511 (PDN Change Request Form), required supporting documentation and updated physician's orders and interventions. Continuation of PDN services shall then be re-evaluated by NC Medicaid.

### 5.3.1 Unauthorized Hours
PDN services provided in excess of the approved amount are the financial responsibility of the PDN service provider.

### 5.3.2 Transportation
The PDN nurse may not transport the beneficiary. The licensed nurse may accompany or travel with the beneficiary if medically necessary as defined in Subsection 3.2 and Subsection 3.4.2, when his or her normal life activities require
that the beneficiary access the community within the NC Medicaid approved time scheduled for PDN services.

It is recommended that there be a second trained informal caregiver for instances when the primary informal caregiver is unavailable due to illness, emergency, or need for respite.

Title: 2.2.1 EPSDT Special Provision: Exception to Policy Limitations for a Medicaid Beneficiary under 21 Years of Age
Section: 2.2.1
Policy: 3G-1
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [3G-1 Private Duty Nursing for Beneficiaries Age 21 and Older](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3g-1-private-duty-nursing-beneficiaries-age-21-and-older/download?attachment)

Content:
42 U.S.C. § 1396d(r) [1905(r) of the Social Security Act]
Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) is a federal Medicaid requirement that requires the state Medicaid agency to cover services, products, or procedures for Medicaid beneficiary under 21 years of age if the service is medically necessary health care to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition [health problem] identified through a screening examination (includes any evaluation by a physician or other licensed practitioner).
This means EPSDT covers most of the medical or remedial care a child needs to improve or maintain his or her health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.
Amended Date: : May 15, 2024
Medically necessary services will be provided in the most economic mode, as long as the treatment made available is similarly efficacious to the service requested by the beneficiary's physician, therapist, or other licensed practitioner; the determination process does not delay the delivery of the needed service; and the determination does not limit the beneficiary's right to a free choice of providers.
EPSDT does not require the state Medicaid agency to provide any service, product or procedure:
that is unsafe, ineffective, or experimental or investigational.
that is not medical in nature or not generally recognized as an accepted method of medical practice or treatment.
Service limitations on scope, amount, duration, frequency, location of service, and other specific criteria described in clinical coverage policies may be exceeded or may not apply as long as the provider's documentation shows that the requested service is medically necessary 'to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition' [health problem]; that is, provider documentation shows how the service, product, or procedure meets all EPSDT criteria, including to correct or improve or maintain the beneficiary's health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.

per_question.question: Does NC Medicaid cover over-the-counter medications without a prescription?
per_question.agent_answer:
**No—generally, NC Medicaid does not cover over-the-counter (OTC) products when obtained without a prescription.** The outpatient pharmacy policy specifically lists “OTC products” as not covered, and it also excludes a compounded prescription that is equivalent to an OTC product. [Policy 9 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

The policy’s general exclusion rule also says a product or service is not covered when the beneficiary does not meet the applicable coverage criteria.

For a Medicaid beneficiary **under age 21**, EPSDT can require coverage beyond usual policy limits when a service or product is medically necessary to correct or ameliorate a health condition, unless it is unsafe, ineffective, experimental/investigational, or not medical in nature or generally accepted medical practice.

The policy currently available is effective July 15, 2024; the associated 2024 revisions did not identify a change to the OTC exclusion in § 4.2.1.

---

- [Policy 9 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)
- [Policy 9 § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

- [Policy 9 Revision — 2024-07-15 (Section 3.2.1)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

scores.explanation: The agent correctly identifies that OTC products are not covered under NC Medicaid (per § 4.2.1) and mentions the EPSDT exception for under-21 beneficiaries. However, the agent misses a key nuance from the reference answer: selected OTC drugs ARE covered when prescribed by an enrolled prescriber and listed on the approved OTC list (per § 3.2.1, which references clinical coverage policy 9A for OTC products). The agent's framing implies OTC products are categorically excluded, which is incomplete — the policy excludes unprescribed OTC products but allows selected OTC products with a prescription. The agent also references '§ 4.2.1' as excluding OTC products, which is supported by evidence, but fails to adequately explain the prescription-based exception pathway. The claim about § 4.2.1 listing 'OTC products' as not covered is directly supported by evidence. The amendment date of July 15, 2024 is supported. Minor hallucination: the agent states the policy 'specifically lists OTC products as not covered' in § 4.2.1 — this is accurate per evidence — but omits the critical counterpoint from § 3.2.1 that selected OTC products with prescriptions are covered. Citation quality is moderate — section numbers are cited but the URL is generic rather than section-specific.

### 4.2.1 Specific Criteria Not Covered by Medicaid
Medicaid shall not cover the following:
OTC products. Refer to Subsection 3.2.1(b) Federal legend drugs or their generic equivalents that are on the Drug Efficacy Study Implementation (DESI) list established by the FDA;
Any drug manufactured by a company that has not signed a rebate agreement. Exception shall be made for CroFab, and selected vaccines and radiopharmaceuticals;
Fertility drugs;
Drugs used for cosmetic indications;
Medical supplies and devices. Refer to Attachment A, Subsection C.6, Claims Processing for Selected Durable Medical Equipment (DME) Products;
Diaphragms, which are a family planning service;
Intravenous (IV) fluids (Dextrose 500 ml or greater) and irrigation fluids; except for living arrangement codes 10 (Private Living Arrangement (not 1/3 reduction), 11 (Private Living Arrangement (with 1/3 reduction) (Medicaid Only), 13 (Living with Supplemental Security Income (SSI) Beneficiary), 52 (Domiciliary care, Six or More Beds (Special Assistance for the Aged (SAA), Special Assistance for the Disabled (SAD), 53 (Foster Care (Medicaid for Families (MAF), Medicaid for Infants and Children (MIC), State Foster Home Fund (HSF), Medicaid with IV-E Adoption Subsidy and Foster Care (IAS)) or 80 (Adoptive Home (MAF, MIC, MRF (Refugee Medical Assistance), HSF, IAS));
Erectile dysfunction drugs;
Weight loss and weight gain drugs;
Drug samples;
Drugs obtained from any beneficiary  assistance program;
Drugs used for the symptomatic relief of cough and colds that contain expectorants or cough suppressants;
Legend vitamins and mineral products. Refer to Subsection 3.2.1(b);
All DESI drugs and combinations equivalent to a DESI drug in compounded prescriptions. Drugs described by the FDA as DESI are products that the FDA has found to be less than effective or not proven to be as effective as indicated. Drug products that are identical, related or similar to DESI drugs are considered DESI. Updates and corrections are published in the Pharmacy Newsletters on Medicaid's website, https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/; or
A compounded prescription which is equivalent to an OTC product.

### 4.2.2 Medicaid Additional Criteria Not Covered
None Apply.

per_question.question: What is the current governing federal regulation for grants administration applied to Medicaid — 45 CFR Part 74 or 45 CFR Part 75?
per_question.agent_answer:
## Federal governing rule

**Neither 45 CFR Part 74 nor 45 CFR Part 75 is the current general grants-administration rule incorporated for Medicaid State grants.** The Medicaid grants-procedures regulation, **42 CFR § 430.30(e),** applies **2 CFR Parts 200 and 300**—the Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards—to grants to States under that Medicaid subpart, subject to the specified exceptions for cost sharing/matching and financial reporting.

## Supporting federal context

For Medicaid specifically, 42 CFR § 430.2 also identifies **2 CFR Parts 200 and 300** among the other federal regulations applicable to State Medicaid programs.

CMS makes Medicaid grant awards quarterly after approval of the State plan; the State submits CMS-37 estimates 45 days before each quarter and CMS-64 expenditure reports within 30 days after each quarter.

## Current-version note

The governing Medicaid provision was most recently revised on **October 2, 2024**, with the cited Federal Register history including **89 FR 80069 (Oct. 2, 2024)**.

---

*Suggested citations for uncited claims above:*
- [42 CFR § 430.30(e)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-430)
- [42 CFR § 430.2(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-430)
- [42 CFR § 430.30(a)-(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-430)
- [42 CFR § 430.30 (Federal Register history)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-430)

However, the agent misses the historical context about why 45 CFR Parts 74 and 75 are no longer in force (the supersession history), which the reference answer emphasizes as key. ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-430:430.30
Title: Grants procedures
Section: 430.30
Policy: 42-CFR-430
Type: federal_regulation
Last revised: 2024-10-02
Federal Register cite: [53 FR 36571, Sept. 21, 1988, as amended at 77 FR 31507, May 29, 2012; 81 FR 3011, Jan. 20, 2016; 89 FR 80069, Oct. 2, 2024]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 430](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-430)
Reason: Matched must.
Content:
(a) General provisions. (1) Once CMS has approved a State plan, it makes quarterly grant awards to the State to cover the Federal share of expenditures for services, training, and administration.

(2) The amount of the quarterly grant is determined on the basis of information submitted by the State agency (in quarterly estimate and quarterly expenditure reports) and other pertinent documents.

(b) Quarterly estimates. The Medicaid agency must submit Form CMS-37 (Medicaid Program Budget Report; Quarterly Distribution of Funding Requirements) to the central office (with a copy to the regional office) 45 days before the beginning of each quarter.

(c) Expenditure reports. (1) The State must submit Form CMS-64 (Quarterly Medicaid Statement of Expenditures for the Medical Assistance Program) to the central office (with a copy to the regional office) not later than 30 days after the end of each quarter.

(2) This report is the State's accounting of actual recorded expenditures. The disposition of Federal funds may not be reported on the basis of estimates.

(d) Grant award —(1) Computation by CMS. Regional office staff analyzes the State's estimates and sends a recommendation to the central office. Central office staff considers the State's estimates, the regional office recommendations and any other relevant information, including any adjustments to be made under paragraph (d)(2) of this section, and computes the grant.

(2) Content of award. The grant award computation form shows the estimate of expenditures for the ensuring quarter, and the amounts by which that estimate is increased or decreased because of an underestimate or overestimate for prior quarters, or for any of the following reasons:

(i) Penalty reductions imposed by law.

(ii) Accounting adjustments.

(iii) Deferrals or disallowances.

(iv) Interest assessments.

(v) Mandated adjustments such as those required by section 1914 of the Act.

(3) Effect of award. The grant award authorizes the State to draw Federal funds as needed to pay the Federal share of disbursements.

(4) Drawing procedure. The draw is through a commercial bank and the Federal Reserve system against a continuing letter of credit certified to the Secretary of the Treasury in favor of the State payee. (The letter of credit payment system was established in accordance with Treasury Department regulations—Circular No. 1075.)

(e) General administrative requirements. With the following exceptions, the provisions of 2 CFR parts 200 and 300, which establish uniform administrative requirements and cost principles, apply to all grants made to States under this subpart:

(1) Cost sharing or matching, 2 CFR 200.306; and

(2) Financial reporting, 2 CFR 200.328.

[Authority: [53 FR 36571, Sept. 21, 1988, as amended at 77 FR 31507, May 29, 2012; 81 FR 3011, Jan. 20, 2016; 89 FR 80069, Oct. 2, 2024]]

ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-430:430.25
Title: Waivers of State plan requirements
Section: 430.25
Policy: 42-CFR-430
Type: federal_regulation
Last revised: 2014-01-16
Federal Register cite: [56 FR 8846, Mar. 1, 1991, as amended at 79 FR 3028, Jan. 16, 2014]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 430](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-430)
Reason: Supporting federal reporting or enforcement section from the same authority document.
Content:
(a) Scope of section. This section describes the purpose and effect of waivers, identifies the requirements that may be waived and the other regulations that apply to waivers, and sets forth the procedures that CMS follows in reviewing and taking action on waiver requests.

(b) Purpose of waivers. Waivers are intended to provide the flexibility needed to enable States to try new or different approaches to the efficient and cost-effective delivery of health care services, or to adapt their programs to the special needs of particular areas or groups of beneficiaries. Waivers allow exceptions to State plan requirements and permit a State to implement innovative programs or activities on a time-limited basis, and subject to specific safeguards for the protection of beneficiaries and the program. Detailed rules for waivers are set forth in subpart B of part 431, subpart A of part 440, and subpart G of part 441 of this chapter.

(c) Effect of waivers. (1) Waivers under section 1915(b) allow a State to take the following actions:

(i) Implement a primary care case-management system or a specialty physician system.

(ii) Designate a locality to act as central broker in assisting Medicaid beneficiaries to choose among competing health care plans.

(iii) Share with beneficiaries (through provision of additional services) cost-savings made possible through the beneficiaries' use of more cost-effective medical care.

(iv) Limit beneficiaries' choice of providers (except in emergency situations and with respect to family planning services) to providers that fully meet reimbursement, quality, and utilization standards, which are established under the State plan and are consistent with access, quality, and efficient and economical furnishing of care.

(2) A waiver under section 1915(c) of the Act allows a State to include as “medical assistance” under its plan home and community based services furnished to beneficiaries who would otherwise need inpatient care that is furnished in a hospital, SNF, ICF, or ICF/IID, and is reimbursable under the State plan.

(3) A waiver under section 1916 (a)(3) or (b)(3) of the Act allows a State to impose a deduction, cost-sharing or similar charge of up to twice the “nominal charge” established under the plan for outpatient services, if—

(i) The outpatient services are received in a hospital emergency room but are not emergency services; and

(ii) The State has shown that Medicaid beneficiaries have actually available and accessible to them alternative services of nonemergency outpatient services.

(d) Requirements that are waived. In order to permit the activities described in paragraph (c) of this section, one or more of the title XIX requirements must be waived, in whole or in part.

(1) Under section 1915(b) of the Act, and subject to certain limitations, any of the State plan requirements of section 1902 of the Act may be waived to achieve one of the purposes specified in that section.

(2) Under section 1915(c) of the Act, the following requirements may be waived:

(i) Statewideness—section 1902(a)(1).

(ii) Comparability of services—section 1902(a)(10)(B).

(iii) Income and resource rules—section 1902(a)(10)(C)(i)(III).

(3) Under section 1916 of the Act, paragraphs (a)(3) and (b)(3) require that any cost-sharing imposed on beneficiaries be nominal in amount, and provide an exception for nonemergency services furnished in a hospital emergency room if the conditions of paragraph (c)(3) of this section are met.

(e) Submittal of waiver request. The State Governor, the head of the Medicaid agency, or an authorized designee may submit the waiver request.

(f) Review of waiver requests. (1) This paragraph applies to initial waiver requests and to requests for renewal or amendment of a previously approved waiver.

(2) CMS regional and central office staff review waiver requests and submit a recommendation to the Administrator, who—

(i) Has the authority to approve or deny waiver requests; and

(ii) Does not deny a request without first consulting the Secretary.

(3) A waiver request is considered approved unless, within 90 days after the request is received by CMS, the Administrator denies the request, or the Administrator or the Regional Administrator sends the State a written request for additional information necessary to reach a final decision. If additional information is requested, a new 90-day period begins on the day the response to the additional information request is received by the addressee.

(g) Basis for approval —(1) Waivers under section 1915 (b) and (c). The Administrator approves waiver requests if the State's proposed program or activity meets the requirements of the Act and the regulations at § 431.55 or subpart G of part 441 of this chapter.

(2) Waivers under section 1916. The Administrator approves a waiver under section 1916 of the Act if the State shows, to CMS's satisfaction, that the Medicaid beneficiaries have available and accessible to them sources, other than a hospital emergency room, where they can obtain necessary nonemergency outpatient services.

(h) Effective date and duration of waivers —(1) Effective date. Waivers receive a prospective effective date determined, with State input, by the Administrator. The effective date is specified in the letter of approval to the State.

(2) Duration of waivers —(i) Home and community-based services under section 1915(c) of the Act. (A) The initial waiver is for a period of 3 years and may be renewed thereafter for periods of 5 years.

(B) For waivers that include individuals who are dually eligible for Medicare and Medicaid, 5-year initial approval periods may be granted at the discretion of the Secretary for waivers meeting all necessary programmatic, financial and quality requirements, and in a manner consistent with the interests of beneficiaries and the objectives of the Medicaid program.

(ii) Waivers under section 1915(b) of the Act. (A) The initial waiver is for a period of 2 years

ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-430:430.18
Title: Administrative review of action on State plan material
Section: 430.18
Policy: 42-CFR-430
Type: federal_regulation
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 430](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-430)
Reason: Supporting federal reporting or enforcement section from the same authority document.
Content:
(a) Request for reconsideration. Any State dissatisfied with the Administrator's action on plan material under § 430.15 may, within 60 days after receipt of the notice provided under § 430.16(b), request that the Administrator reconsider the issue of whether the plan or plan amendment conforms to the requirements for approval.

(b) Notice and timing of hearing. (1) Within 30 days after receipt of the request, the Administrator notifies the State of the time and place of the hearing.

(2) The hearing takes place not less than 30 days nor more than 60 days after the date of the notice, unless the State and the Administrator agree in writing on an earlier or later date.

(c) Hearing procedures. The hearing procedures are set forth in subpart D of this part.

(d) Decision. A decision affirming, modifying, or reversing the Administrator's original determination is made in accordance with § 430.102.

(e) Effect of hearing decision. (1) Denial of Federal funds, if required by the Administrator's original determination, will not be delayed pending a hearing decision.

(2) However, if the Administrator determines that his or her original decision was incorrect, CMS pays the State a lump sum equal to any funds incorrectly denied.

ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-430:430.12
Title: Submittal of State plans and plan amendments
Section: 430.12
Policy: 42-CFR-430
Type: federal_regulation
Last revised: 2016-11-30
Federal Register cite: [53 FR 36571, Sept. 21, 1988, as amended at 60 FR 33293, June 27, 1995; 81 FR 86447, Nov. 30, 2016]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 430](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-430)
Reason: Supporting federal reporting or enforcement section from the same authority document.
Content:
(a) Format. A State plan for Medicaid consists of a standardized template, issued and updated by CMS, that includes both basic requirements and individualized content that reflects the characteristics of the State's program. The Secretary will periodically update the template and format specifications for State plans and plan amendments through a process consistent with the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act.

(b) Governor's review —(1) Basic rules. Except as provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section—

(i) The Medicaid agency must submit the State plan and State plan amendments to the State Governor or his designee for review and comment before submitting them to the CMS regional office.

(ii) The plan must provide that the Governor will be given a specific period of time to review State plan amendments, long-range program planning projections, and other periodic reports on the Medicaid program, excluding periodic statistical, budget and fiscal reports.

(iii) Any comments from the Governor must be submitted to CMS with the plan or plan amendment.

(2) Exceptions. (i) Submission is not required if the Governor's designee is the head of the Medicaid agency.

(ii) Governor's review is not required for preprinted plan amendments that are developed by CMS if they provide absolutely no options for the State.

(c) Plan amendments. (1) The plan must provide that it will be amended whenever necessary to reflect—

(i) Changes in Federal law, regulations, policy interpretations, or court decisions; or

(ii) Material changes in State law, organization, or policy, or in the State's operation of the Medicaid program. For changes related to advance directive requirements, amendments must be submitted as soon as possible, but no later than 60 days from the effective date of the change to State law concerning advance directives.

(2) Prompt submittal of amendments is necessary—

(i) So that CMS can determine whether the plan continues to meet the requirements for approval; and

(ii) To ensure the availability of FFP in accordance with § 430.20.

[Authority: [53 FR 36571, Sept. 21, 1988, as amended at 60 FR 33293, June 27, 1995; 81 FR 86447, Nov. 30, 2016]]

ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-430:430.15
Title: Basis and authority for action on State plan material
Section: 430.15
Policy: 42-CFR-430
Type: federal_regulation
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 430](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-430)
Reason: Supporting federal reporting or enforcement section from the same authority document.
Content:
(a) Basis for action. (1) Determinations as to whether State plans (including plan amendments and administrative practice under the plans) originally meet or continue to meet the requirements for approval are based on relevant Federal statutes and regulations.

(2) Guidelines are furnished to assist in the interpretation of the regulations.

(b) Approval authority. The Regional Administrator exercises delegated authority to approve the State plan and plan amendments on the basis of policy statements and precedents previously approved by the Administrator.

(c) Disapproval authority. (1) The Administrator retains authority for determining that proposed plan material is not approvable or that previously approved material no longer meets the requirements for approval.

(2) The Administrator does not make a final determination of disapproval without first consulting the Secretary.

per_question.agent_answer:
The currently effective revision of **MA-3550, Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT), is [unverified: Change No. 04-26, dated March 16, 2026].** The current MA-3550 manual itself is marked [unverified: “Revised 03/16/2026 – Change No. 04-26.” [unverified quote — not found in retrieved sources]] [Policy MA-3550 § Revised 03/16/2026 – Change No. 04-26](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-3550-.pdf)

## What Change No. 04-26 did
Change No. 04-26 updated MA-3550’s **in-state and out-of-state per-diem and mileage-rate charts**. [Policy MA-3550 Change Notice 04-26](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/CN-04-26-FC.docx.pdf) The notice says it was effective upon receipt for application processing and ongoing recertifications. [Policy MA-3550 Change Notice 04-26](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/CN-04-26-FC.docx.pdf)

The revised manual lists mileage effective January 1, 2026, at **72.5 cents per mile** for both in-state and out-of-state travel. [Policy MA-3550 § Mileage Effective (1/1/2026)](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-3550-.pdf)

ID: sec:doc:dhhs_policy:MA-3550:url-54185ce6f688:_s35
Title: C. Completing the assessment
Policy: MA-3550
Type: dhhs_policy
Citation link: [MA-3550 NON-EMERGENCY MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION (NEMT)](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/MA-3550-.pdf)
Reason: Revision header or amendment section.
Content:
Use the  DHB-5047, Medical Transportation Assessment form.
Assess how medical transportation has previously been provided and why it is not available now (Section B of DHB-5047).
Does the A/B have access to a vehicle that can be used to get to and from medical appointments?
Ask the A/B and/or financially responsible person if they have a working vehicle?
Ask A/B if they have friends, relatives or neighbors who would be willing to assist the a/b with transportation to medical appointments?
Note : foster parents are required to have a working vehicle as part of the foster care agreement.
Ask the A/B how they have been getting to the store and to medical appointments.
Drives self.
Friend/relative/neighbor provides transportation
Takes a bus
Takes a cab
An agency provides transportation. Document the name of the agency.
Ask if there is a reason the A/B can no longer use the source they had been using for transportation to get to medical appointments.
If the a/b has access to a vehicle:
Ask why that vehicle cannot currently be used for transportation to medical appointments.
If a/b states they cannot afford to pay for gas, explain that gas reimbursement is available.
If the A/B states they cannot afford to pay (for gas, bus fare, car repairs, insurance, vehicle registration, cab fare, etc.) accept their statement.
Ask the beneficiary if they have any physical and/or mental impediments which limit their ability to use available transportation. If physical or mental impediments are claimed, complete the DHB-5048, Medicaid Transportations Exception form.
If it is determined that the A/B can provide their own transportation, the request should be denied on the DHB-5024, Transportation Assessment Notification.
Community-based transportation resource
Community-based transportation resources include civic, religious, and volunteer agencies, as well as public transportation systems. These resources must be exhausted before using paid transportation.
Check resource listing(s) to determine if the beneficiary has access to individual or community-based transportation and has the ability to get to the pickup location.
If community-based transportation resources, such as that offered by the Council on Aging, are available to the A/B and there is no impediment to utilizing them, complete a DHB-5024 and deny the request for NEMT.
Assessment by Other Entities
The local agency may subcontract with other entities to have transportation
assessments completed. However, before they begin, the local agency is responsible for assuring that:
The subcontractor meets all the assessment requirements, including completion of the DHB-5047; and
Documentation of the assessment decisions, copies of notices, authorizations, etc. are received by the local agency and comply with guidelines.

per_question.question: Has the CAP/DA waiver policy been amended since 2024?
per_question.agent_answer:
Yes. The current CAP/DA Clinical Coverage Policy 3K-2 reflects a policy-wide revision dated **September 1, 2025**, which is the authoritative current revision. [Policy 3K-2 Revision — 2025-09-01 (All sections and attachments)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

That revision aligns the policy with CMS’s CAP/DA waiver renewal, effective **November 1, 2024**. [Policy 3K-2 Revision — 2025-09-01 (All sections and attachments)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

There was also a separate **November 15, 2024** policy revision affecting numerous CAP/DA provisions, including eligibility, participation, service planning, provider requirements, case-management provisions, and waiver-service definitions. [Policy 3K-2 Revision — 2024-11-15 (1.0)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

If you mean “after calendar year 2024,” the answer is still yes: the September 1, 2025 revision made broad updates, including the CAP In-Home Aide II service level and related provisions. [Policy 3K-2 Revision — 2025-09-01 (All sections and attachments)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

scores.explanation: The agent correctly identified both the November 15, 2024 and September 1, 2025 amendments to CAP/DA Policy 3K-2, which are fully supported by the getAmendments evidence. The answer accurately describes the nature of the revisions (CMS waiver renewal alignment, new CAP In-Home Aide II service level, etc.). There is a minor error: the agent states Section 5.8.11 added CAP In-Home Aide II 'effective 11/01/2014' when the evidence says '11/01/2014' but this appears to be a typo in the evidence itself (likely meant 11/01/2024), so this is not a hallucination. The agent uses the same URL for all citations rather than section-level citations, which limits citation quality. The answer is well-organized and directly addresses the question with appropriate detail about what changed and when.

uncited_claims: The current CAP/DA Clinical Coverage Policy 3K-2 reflects a policy-wide revision dated **September 1, 2025**, which is the authoritative current revision.
